summary:
Held 2 of today's 10 biggest UK/EU movers.

• 4 upside misses — BARC.L +4%, AKZA.AS +4%, CA.PA +4%, AALB.AS +3%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (BAB.L -6%, BRBY.L -3%, BA.L -2%, TEP.PA -2%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: BAB.L (-5.89%) — Audited annual-report detail crystallised ~£700M of outstanding Type 31 Royal Navy frigate costs; a 10% cost variance implies a ~£70M swing, overwhelming the £200M buyback announced alongside May results. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe — BAB.L is a UK defense/industrial contractor (FTSE 250) not covered by current sector filters. The move was also a secondary re-rating of a previously disclosed charge (May 13), not a fresh breakout signal, so news-reactive systems had no new trigger to fire on.

top_movers.catalyst: Bernstein lifted IFX PT from EUR 74 to EUR 102 (Outperform) after EU close on Jun 22; compounded by a European semiconductor sector relief rally as names recovered from the Jun 5 Broadcom-triggered oversell.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any strategy's universe — IFX.DE is a large-cap DAX semiconductor not in EU filters. The move combined a post-EU-close Bernstein PT raise with sector mean-reversion; pre-market positioning is needed to catch this pattern.
top_movers.suggestion: Expand macro-aligned's EU universe to include DAX/MDAX semiconductor names and add a post-EU-close analyst PT-raise gate (≥20% target increase) that flags for pre-market limit entry at next open.

top_movers.catalyst: UK PM Keir Starmer's resignation triggered a broad FTSE 100 financial sector rally; NatWest +4%, Barclays and Lloyds both ~+3.8%, amplified by a BofA price-target upgrade to 600p on 21 June.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — BARC.L is a FTSE 100 mega-cap UK bank. Move was sector-wide co-movement triggered by PM Starmer's resignation (intraday political catalyst); no pre-market signal could have positioned ahead of it.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a FTSE 100 large-cap financials sleeve (BARC, LLOY, NWG, HSBA) to a macro/sector rotation strategy, gated on intraday breadth: trigger when ≥3 of the 4 names are up >1.5% by 10:00 BST with financials leading the index.

top_movers.catalyst: Morgan Stanley initiated coverage on 22-Jun with Overweight and €20.10 PT (≈22% upside), citing faster-than-expected restructuring execution, 11% EPS CAGR to 2028, ~14% FCF yield, and a 40% P/E discount to EU retail peers.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — CA.PA is a €11B EU large-cap consumer-staples retailer not covered by the bot's filters. The trigger was a tier-1 broker initiation published after Monday's close; no pre-open momentum or mean-reversion signal existed before Tuesday's gap-up.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a broker-initiation gate to a news-reactive strategy: for EU large-cap consumer/retail names, open a small position at next-session open when a tier-1 bank initiates Overweight with implied upside ≥20% and prior-session volume is within normal range.

top_movers.catalyst: Besi's June 18 Investor Day raised long-term revenue targets to €1.7–2.2B on surging AI/2.5D packaging demand; analyst price-target upgrades published in the days following continued to re-rate the stock into today's close.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. BESI is a Dutch semi-equipment mid-cap specialising in hybrid bonding/advanced packaging not covered by current screeners; the +3.3% gain was a slow-burn post-investor-day re-rating requiring pre-event positioning to capture.
top_movers.suggestion: Add EU semiconductor-equipment peers (BESI.AS, ASMI.AS) to macro-aligned-macro-attn's universe with an investor-day or raised-guidance event flag that opens a 3-session entry window post-announcement.

top_movers.catalyst: Aalberts N.V. rejoined the AEX index effective 22 Jun 2026 (Euronext quarterly review), driving index-tracker fund inflows on the first full trading session after inclusion.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. AALB.AS is a Dutch large-cap industrial; the +2.95% move reflects forced passive-fund buying on day-1 of AEX re-inclusion — a structural corporate-action event not captured by price/volume momentum or mean-reversion signals.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a Euronext quarterly-review event filter: auto-enroll newly confirmed AEX/AMX entrants into the news-reactive strategy's universe for the 3 trading sessions following the effective inclusion date.

top_movers.catalyst: Audited annual-report detail crystallised ~£700M of outstanding Type 31 Royal Navy frigate costs; a 10% cost variance implies a ~£70M swing, overwhelming the £200M buyback announced alongside May results.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — BAB.L is a UK defense/industrial contractor (FTSE 250) not covered by current sector filters. The move was also a secondary re-rating of a previously disclosed charge (May 13), not a fresh breakout signal, so news-reactive systems had no new trigger to fire on.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a 'delayed_risk_reassessment' screen: LSE defense/industrial names with unresolved material charges >£100M in the prior 60 days showing renewed >3% single-day weakness should be auto-admitted to the news-reactive universe for that session.

top_movers.catalyst: New Fed Chair Warsh's surprise hawkish rate signal on 23 Jun triggered a global risk-off; FTSE 100 fell ~0.76% and European luxury sold off in sympathy — no Burberry-specific RNS or earnings catalyst.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — BRBY.L is a mid-cap UK luxury name (~£3.8bn mkt cap). The -2.82% decline was pure macro/sector contagion with no company RNS, earnings surprise, or pre-market volume spike to trigger a momentum or news-reactive entry.
top_movers.suggestion: No actionable change — macro-driven sector contagion with no stock-specific signal; capturing this type of move requires short capability and a Fed-sentiment overlay that is outside current strategy scope.

top_movers.catalyst: Babcock FY results (19% op-profit drop, £140M Type 31 frigate charge) spread UK defence sector contagion; US-Iran ceasefire road map (talks concluded June 21) simultaneously stripped the geopolitical risk premium from European defence names.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. BA.L is a FTSE 100 mega-cap defence prime (~£55B mkt cap); the decline was a gradual multi-day macro de-rating from geopolitical de-risking and peer contagion — not an event-driven gap that pre-open news or momentum signals could front-run.
top_movers.suggestion: If short capability exists, add a 'geopolitical de-risk short' gate for FTSE 100 defence names: trigger when a ceasefire/peace MoU is confirmed in the news feed AND STOXX Aerospace & Defence index is down >1.5% pre-open, allowing a short entry sized at ≤0.5% NAV.

top_movers.catalyst: No specific breaking catalyst on 2026-06-23; likely continued BPO sector de-rating on AI displacement fears, amplified by TEP's Q1 2026 revenue miss (−2.2% LFL) and persistent analyst downgrades from Citi and Morgan Stanley.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. TEP.PA is a French mid-cap (~€3.1B) in deep structural decline (>80% drawdown from 2022 peak), disqualified from momentum screens; capturing further downside requires short capability the bot does not have.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a 'fallen-large-cap watchlist' tier for ex-CAC 40 names with mkt cap €1–5B and 52-week return < −50% to surface for short-side review; no actionable long-only change — this move is only capturable with short capability.
